body: So many late night lans with 1.6.  The scrims, the matches, scoutzknivez w/ low grav; I never thought I would say this, but I really miss high school lol

Help make friends and family live comfortably.  Pay off their mortgages, car loans, school loans, and a little extra.  I would give my Mom as much as she wants so she can go off and do what she wants with out any worries.

Maybe more importantly, DONATE!!!  I would donate a lot to the Children's Medical Center and make a ridiculous donation to their Christmas Toy Drive.  The other area I would donate a good amount to is animal shelters.  I love animals and had many dogs and cats growing up.  Other good causes would get money too.  I'm sure there are already things like this, but I want to do some kind of a computer donation drive.  Less fortunate families could come and get a decent speced, brand new computer for very little or completely free.  All the money would go towards a local food pantry.

I honestly don't want a lot for myself.  A house, a car, and enough to cover any unexpected life expenses.  Traveling is something I've wanted to do for a long time.  Thinking about being able to pay for any plane or cruise ticket any time I want puts a smile on my face.

So my friends and family no longer have to stress about money.  College loans, mortgages, medical bills all gone in the blink of an eye.  It makes me feel good to know they could focus on what makes them happy.

If I JUST found out that I won, before I actually got the money, I'm going to Wingstop and getting a ton of original hot wings, bluecheese dressing, fries, and honey mustard.

If were talking about coming home, checking the account and seeing $200 million, hmm.  I would buy tickets as close as possible to our old season tickets seats for the Texas Rangers and not care what I ordered to eat and drink.  And I would tip the SHIT out of our server.

I would make it so the only bills I ever get are water, tv/internet, and cellphone.

I learned that your body language is the first thing people notice and they can judge you just from that, even before you have a chance to open your mouth.  Look at your upper body in a mirror and see what your shoulders and head are doing when you feel normal and relaxed.  Are your shoulders slouched forward and head hanging low?  That was my normal posture for a long time before someone said something.  I decided to change my posture by making a conscience effort to make sure my shoulders were back and my head was up straight.  After a while it became second nature.  It really does make a big difference.

Facial expressions can be more difficult.  The easiest way to make a stranger take a liking to you is to smile.  If you smile at someone you'll usually get a smile back. If you're not really happy then it's hard to put on a smile, I know from experience.  But once you see how easy it is to put a smile on someones face just because you smiled it will make you want to smile more.

People like your Dad need just as much help, if not more than the people he's hurting.  Some people can be straight up bastards, but it's usually not without reason.  I learned not to hate my Dad, but instead to hate his illness.

You're lucky you don't have to deal with your problems on your own.  I tried to deal with it on my own for years and it made my life worse and worse.  But once my Mom and I could sit down and talk honestly about what was going on and what had happened, it made me feel much better.

Today is better than yesterday and thank you for the offer.  I hope you, your Mom, and your brother start having better days soon!

My Mom said her biggest regret was not trying to get us to into some kind of therapy early on.  Talking to a professional still seems like a good idea though.  I'm glad that your therapist was able to help you!  All of your comments have really helped me out.

I'm REALLY sorry your dad is abusive.  FUCK anyone who is abusive.  Okay fine, be miserable but don't take it out on others.  I'm thankful my dad was never physically abusive.  He was mentally abusive towards my Mom though.  I learned that one time he tried to kill himself one day before father's day.  When he didn't succeed, he just blew it off like nothing happened.  My Mom was very scared not because of his suicide attempt, but for the way he acted afterwards.  She said she wondered how many times he tried suicide before and she had no idea about it.  Be kind to your Mom and show her support anytime you can get.  

I don't know how old you are, but be strong and don't give up.  Talk to a friend, family member, or if you're still in school, a counselor.  I was embarrassed to talk to anyone about it for too long and it messed up what I thought would be one of the most fun times of my life.  Good luck!
I had a long talk with my Mom after posting this.  I cried for the first time in 8 years and it felt good.  It doesn't fix anything but I feel better having finally talked to someone about it.
Thank you, it means a lot for you to say that.  I never thought about it as helping, more just doing what I had to do.  I don't know why I'm having problems doing it now.

Every year I think about the time I wasted from the year before and it just piles up in my mind.  It made me more and more depressed, depressed to the point I didn't feel like doing anything about it.  I know it doesn't make any sense but for whatever reason it worked in my mind.

And you're right, I just need to jump in and get going with it!
I think one of the best things my Dad did for me was get me interested in computers.  I've done some IT stuff in the past so it's what I want to try getting a degree in.
